comments.document:
Now that I'm reviewing all the material for finals, I came across a few sites that I thought would be useful for us. Sharing them here in case they help anyone else!

Lilian Weng's Blog (lilianweng.github.io): This is honestly one of the best resources I've found. She's a researcher at OpenAI and her posts are incredibly thorough with clean math and great diagrams. A few standouts:

"Attention? Attention!" - Covers the evolution of attention mechanisms from seq2seq to transformers: https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2018-06-24-attention/

"The Transformer Family Version 2.0" - A comprehensive survey of transformer variants (sparse attention, efficient transformers, etc.): https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2023-01-27-the-transformer-family-v2/

"Why We Think" (new, May 2025) - Deep dive into test-time compute and chain-of-thought, which connects nicely to Lecture 25: https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2025-05-01-thinking/


3Blue1Brown's Deep Learning Series: Grant Sanderson recently extended his neural network series to cover transformers and LLMs. The visualizations are incredible for building intuition:

Transformers chapter: https://www.3blue1brown.com/lessons/gpt

Attention step-by-step: https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/neural-networks

The way he visualizes attention as queries, keys, and values really clicked for me when I was reviewing the multi-head attention lecture.

CNN Explainer: Interactive visualization for understanding CNNs. You can see exactly how convolutions, pooling, and activation functions transform the input at each layer. Really helped solidify my understanding from Lecture 11. https://poloclub.github.io/cnn-explainer/

CVPR 2022 Diffusion Models Tutorial: For anyone wanting to go deeper on Lecture 27 (diffusion models), this tutorial from CVPR has slides, video, and covers both DDPM and score-based perspectives: https://cvpr2022-tutorial-diffusion-models.github.io/

UvA Deep Learning Notebooks: Full Jupyter notebooks with PyTorch implementations and explanations. Their Transformer tutorial is particularly good and includes the warm-up learning rate discussion that came up in lecture: https://uvadlc-notebooks.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorial_notebooks/tutorial6/Transformers_and_MHAttention.html

LearnOpenCV DDPM Tutorial : If you want to actually implement diffusion models from scratch in PyTorch, this is a great walkthrough with code: https://learnopencv.com/denoising-diffusion-probabilistic-models/

Hope some of these help! Good luck with finals everyone 🙏
